standard: RHS Colour Chart fifth edition; Saccardo Chromotaxia 1891
recognition_definition: A source-qualified cream observation is recognized against its named standard: by closest match to RHS fifth-edition chip 158A or 158B under the stated comparison protocol, or by Saccardo category 27 and its cow-milk-cream exemplar.
ontology_recommendation: Retain PATO:0104031 as generic cream and add the RHS and Saccardo standards as FLOPO-local sensu children; keep unrestricted creamy on the PATO parent.
caveat: The physical RHS chips are normative for the RHS child; display RGB values are not. Unqualified PATO:0104031 annotations remain on the generic parent; explicit RHS annotations use the FLOPO child.

standard: Wilson Horticultural Colour Chart; Textile Color Card Association of the USA; Ridgway 1912 comparison with the 1886 Nomenclature
standard_designation: Wilson H22; TCCA Crimson (USA) 65013; older Crimson approximately unprinted Plate I coordinate 1j
recognition_definition: A source-qualified crimson observation is recognized by closest match to Wilson H22 or TCCA card 65013; Ridgway's comparison places the older 1886 name approximately at unprinted coordinate 1j and explicitly reports no matching 1912 chip.
ontology_recommendation: Create a generic PATO crimson umbrella plus Wilson H22 and TCCA 65013 FLOPO-local sensu children; retain the older Ridgway comparison as unresolved evidence rather than an operational child.
caveat: NIST places the Wilson and TCCA senses in different ISCC-NBS blocks, and the Ridgway approximate coordinate is not itself a printed prototype chip.

standard: Saccardo Chromotaxia 1891; Ridgway 1912; Wilson Horticultural Colour Chart
standard_designation: Saccardo category 15; Ridgway Scarlet I 5; Wilson H19
recognition_definition: A source-qualified scarlet observation is recognized by the named Saccardo category, Ridgway chip, or Wilson chart chip; these are preserved as separate operational senses.
ontology_recommendation: Create one open generic PATO scarlet umbrella and three FLOPO-local sensu children. Optionally expose a separately named closed union of the current reviewed children; do not close the generic umbrella.
caveat: Unqualified scarlet maps to the umbrella. Degree-modified forms require explicit modifier semantics. Sensu children are not disjoint merely because the standards differ.

recognition_definition: A surface is silver-coloured in this standard when it appears white and has metallic lustre, as represented by Saccardo category 1.
ontology_recommendation: Model a FLOPO appearance composition using a pale/white colour component plus a reflectivity or metallic-lustre component; do not reduce all silvery structures to grey.
caveat: Pale hairs, wax, bloom, and specular reflection can all cause a silvery field appearance. Saccardo's physical plate is historic and may have aged.

standard_designation: Saccardo category 22 gold-yellow; Ridgway Old Gold XVI 19-prime-i = Munsell 3.5Y 5.5/6.0
recognition_definition: A surface is gold-yellow in Saccardo when it has the egg-yellow colour with added splendour; Old Gold in Ridgway is recognized by the named chip corresponding approximately to Munsell 3.5Y 5.5/6.0 in Hamly's key.
ontology_recommendation: Keep unqualified golden as a FLOPO appearance composition or contextual source expression; a source-qualified Ridgway value could be proposed separately.
caveat: Golden may assert yellow hue, metallic/specular lustre, maturation, or drying. Hamly states that the conversion preserves legacy data and is not recommended for new observations.

standard_designation: Saccardo category 24 lemon-yellow; Ridgway Lemon Yellow IV 23 = Munsell 7.5Y 8.0/10.5
recognition_definition: A surface is lemon-yellow in Saccardo when it matches the epicarp of Citrus medica or Citrus limon; in Ridgway it is recognized by chip IV 23, approximately Munsell 7.5Y 8.0/10.5.
ontology_recommendation: Create a generic PATO lemon-yellow umbrella plus separate Saccardo category 24 and Ridgway IV 23 FLOPO-local sensu children; require colour context for lemon alone.
caveat: Natural citrus epicarp varies, and Ridgway's chip is a different reproducible historical standard.

recognition_definition: A surface is mahogany red in this standard when its closest match is Ridgway Mahogany Red II 7k, corresponding approximately to Munsell 10R 3.5/6.0.
ontology_recommendation: Create a generic PATO mahogany-red umbrella and a Ridgway II 7k FLOPO-local sensu child; use the child prototype when repairing FLOPO:0980154 only if the source names Ridgway.
caveat: The unqualified word mahogany can name wood or a broader family of brown-red colours.

standard_designation: Saccardo category 16 salmon-coloured; Ridgway Salmon Color XIV 9-prime-d = Munsell 5YR 7.5/6.0
recognition_definition: A surface is salmon-coloured in Saccardo when it resembles salmon flesh; in Ridgway it is recognized by chip XIV 9-prime-d, approximately Munsell 5YR 7.5/6.0.
ontology_recommendation: Create a generic PATO salmon-colour umbrella plus separate Saccardo and Ridgway FLOPO-local sensu children; model pale salmon-pink composition in FLOPO.
caveat: Salmon flesh varies and pale salmon-pink additionally contains a degree modifier and pink composition.

standard_designation: Saccardo category 10 chestnut-coloured; Ridgway Chestnut II 9m = Munsell 10R 3.0/5.0; Chestnut-Brown XIV 11-prime-m = 2.5YR 3.4/3.0
recognition_definition: A surface is chestnut-coloured in Saccardo when it resembles the pericarp or seed coat of Castanea sativa; Ridgway distinguishes a redder Chestnut chip and a browner Chestnut-Brown chip with the stated Munsell approximations.
ontology_recommendation: Create a generic PATO chestnut-colour umbrella plus Saccardo, Ridgway Chestnut, and Ridgway Chestnut-Brown FLOPO-local sensu children.
caveat: The two Ridgway chips demonstrate that chestnut alone does not determine one hue/value/chroma region.

standard_designation: Saccardo category 10 chocolate-brown; Ridgway Chocolate XXVIII 7-double-prime-m = Munsell 2.5YR 2.6/2.5
recognition_definition: A surface is chocolate-brown in Saccardo when it resembles roasted seeds of Theobroma cacao; in Ridgway it is recognized by chip XXVIII 7-double-prime-m, approximately Munsell 2.5YR 2.6/2.5.
ontology_recommendation: Create a generic PATO chocolate-brown umbrella plus separate Saccardo and Ridgway FLOPO-local sensu children; require colour context for chocolate alone.
caveat: Cacao roast and commercial chocolate products vary in colour.

standard_designation: Saccardo category 39 olive-green; Ridgway Olive XXX 21-double-prime-m = Munsell 5Y 3.8/3.0; Olive-Green IV 23m = 7.5Y 4.0/3.5
recognition_definition: An olive or olive-green observation is recognized only against the selected standard chip; Ridgway explicitly distinguishes Olive from Olive-Green with the stated Munsell approximations.
ontology_recommendation: Create a generic PATO olive-colour umbrella plus separate Saccardo, Ridgway Olive, and Ridgway Olive-Green FLOPO-local sensu children; keep PATO:0001942 olive green only as a related lexical mapping.
caveat: The Saudi olive occurrence is primarily resemblance/shape prose, and historic standards assign multiple distinct olive regions.

standard_designation: Saccardo category 17 rosy; Ridgway Rose Color XII 71b = Munsell 5RP 5.5/14.0; Rose Pink XII 71f = 5RP 8.0/8.0
recognition_definition: A surface is rosy in Saccardo when it resembles petals of typical Rosa centifolia; Ridgway distinguishes saturated Rose Color from lighter Rose Pink using the stated chips and Munsell approximations.
ontology_recommendation: Create a generic PATO rose-colour umbrella plus separate Saccardo, Ridgway Rose Color, and Ridgway Rose Pink FLOPO-local sensu children; reuse corrected PATO:0001425 as the generic parent.
caveat: Rose is also a taxon/common noun, and actual rose petals span many colours.

standard_designation: Saccardo category 26 straw-coloured; Ridgway Straw Yellow XVI 21-prime-d = Munsell 6Y 8.4/6.0
recognition_definition: A surface is straw-coloured in Saccardo when it resembles freshly dried culms of wheat or rice; in Ridgway it is recognized by chip XVI 21-prime-d, approximately Munsell 6Y 8.4/6.0.
ontology_recommendation: Create a generic PATO straw-yellow umbrella plus separate Saccardo and Ridgway FLOPO-local sensu children; require colour context for straw alone.
caveat: Dried culms vary with species, age, and preservation; the Ridgway chip is the more reproducible historical prototype.
